transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we go further on the assignment package. While reviewing the original license from the vendor's legacy contract archive, I found an anti-assignment clause that requires the vendor's prior written consent — and specifically, that consent must name the buyer as the permitted successor. This clause was omitted from the circulated contract abstract, so it hasn't been reflected in the approval materials or the assignment draft yet. This means the current draft transferring software rights to the buyer at closing could trigger a breach unless we obtain a properly executed consent from the vendor naming the buyer before closing.

transcript.text: I confirmed with the division's operations lead yesterday that the buyer needs uninterrupted access to the platform for exactly 120 days after closing while its replacement system is configured. That operational requirement has not yet been added to the transition schedule, and it's directly relevant to Marcus's point — any consent we obtain from the vendor needs to cover not just the assignment itself but also this 120-day continued access period, or the buyer could face a gap in platform availability right after closing.

transcript.text: Thank you both — Marcus, Nina, this is exactly why I asked you to flag conditions and operational protections before I approve this package. Marcus, the anti-assignment clause requiring the vendor's prior written consent naming the buyer as permitted successor is a hard blocker — we cannot let the current draft go forward as-is. Nina, the 120-day continued access requirement is equally critical; if the vendor's consent doesn't explicitly cover that post-closing access period, we're creating an operational gap for the buyer. Before I sign off on the assignment package, I need two things: first, the assignment draft must be revised to condition effectiveness on receipt of the vendor's properly executed consent naming the buyer as successor; second, that consent must also expressly cover the 120-day uninterrupted platform access period Nina described. I also want the transition schedule updated to reflect that 120-day access requirement. Can both of you confirm whether there are any other conditions or protections I should be aware of before I make my decision?
